caption:
Your staff Christmas party probably isn't tax deductible. Here's why that's fine.

The $300 line: if the party (or a gift) costs less than $300 per person and it's occasional, it can be an exempt minor benefit, so no fringe benefits tax.

The trade-off: for entertainment like a party, the ATO's rule is that if it isn't subject to FBT, you can't claim an income tax deduction or GST credits for it.

On your premises, on a working day, current employees only? No FBT on the food and drink. Same trade-off.

So for most small businesses a modest Christmas party is simply a cost: no FBT to pay, nothing to claim. Go over $300 a head and FBT comes into it, which is where a registered tax or BAS agent is worth a call.

What's your team doing this year?

Narrated by an AI voice.

#smallbusinessaustralia #christmasparty #fbt #taxdeductions #keepmore
figures_checked: Christmas party on business premises on a working day for current employees only: no FBT on food and drink; off-site party or gifts under $300 per person can be an exempt minor benefit; where no FBT applies, no income tax deduction or GST credits for the entertainment (ATO Common entertainment scenarios for business; Minor benefits exemption, checked 15 Nov 2026)
